issues.legal_issue: A transfer within the land-ceiling law’s lookback period is made in good faith without proof that it was required by an impelling or pressing necessity when it is a genuine, irrevocable transfer made in the ordinary management of the transferor’s affairs and is not a device to evade the ceiling restriction.
material_facts: The tenure-holder sold two parcels of land under registered sale deeds for adequate consideration and handed possession to the purchasers.
The authority did not find that the sales were fictitious or benami, that the purchasers lacked possession, or that the tenure-holder retained an interest in the land.

The sales were made to raise funds to acquire a site and construct a residence; the authority rejected the claimed good faith solely because it considered the construction insufficiently urgent or necessary.

The transfers were made during the period covered by the statutory lookback rule, and the other stated conditions concerning consideration, irrevocability, and absence of benefit to the tenure-holder or family were not disputed.
issues.conclusion: Proof of an impelling need or pressing legal necessity is not an indispensable requirement of good faith. The transfers qualified for the proviso’s protection, and the authorities had to take them into account when redetermining the tenure-holder’s ceiling area.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5(6), proviso (b), of the Uttar Pradesh Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, as amended by the 1972 Amendment Act, a qualifying transfer within the lookback period is not ignored when determining surplus land. Explanation II places the burden on the party claiming the benefit to prove that the case falls within the proviso. Read with Section 5(1), “good faith” means a bona fide transfer in the ordinary course of managing the transferor’s affairs, genuinely and irrevocably divesting the transferor of all rights and interests, including cultivatory possession, without collusion, a design to evade the ceiling restriction, a reserved present or future benefit, or a mere purpose of converting surplus land into cash. Adequate consideration, an irrevocable instrument, and the absence of a benami transaction or family benefit must also be established. Once those matters are established and no suspicious circumstances appear, proof of an impelling need or legal necessity is not additionally required. The Court cited no earlier cases; it referred to Words & Phrases for the ordinary meaning of “good faith.”

rule.if: land_ceiling_assessment and transfer_within_lookback_window and transfer_would_otherwise_be_surplus and ordinary_management_transfer and adequate_consideration and irrevocable_transfer and complete_divestment_including_possession and not benami_or_family_benefit and not collusive_or_evasion_device and not merely_surplus_to_cash

predicates.land_ceiling_assessment: The proceeding determines whether land held by a person exceeds a statutory ceiling.
predicates.transfer_within_lookback_window: The transfer occurred within the period to which the ceiling law’s lookback rule applies.
predicates.transfer_would_otherwise_be_surplus: Apart from the transfer, the land would be treated as surplus in the ceiling assessment.
predicates.ordinary_management_transfer: The transfer was made in the ordinary course of the transferor’s management of personal affairs.
predicates.adequate_consideration: The transferee gave adequate consideration for the land.
predicates.irrevocable_transfer: The transfer was made by an instrument that could not be revoked.
predicates.complete_divestment_including_possession: The transferor genuinely surrendered all rights and interests in the land, including possession, to the transferee.
predicates.benami_or_family_benefit: The transfer was benami or was made for the immediate or deferred benefit of the transferor or a family member.
predicates.collusive_or_evasion_device: The transfer involved collusion or was designed to evade the ceiling restriction.
predicates.merely_surplus_to_cash: The transfer was made merely to convert surplus land into cash.

issues.definition: When a transfer in a land-ceiling assessment falls within the lookback period and would otherwise make land surplus, a genuine, adequately paid, irrevocable transfer in the ordinary management of affairs that fully divests the transferor and is not benami, for family benefit, collusive, evasive, or merely a conversion of surplus land into cash is taken into account in the ceiling calculation, without a separate showing of pressing necessity.
